editorial.marketOverview: Friday's semiconductor-led selloff remains the latest US cash-market observation: Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite -5.28% and SOX roughly -11%, while AP's November 21 recap reports Nasdaq -5.3% and S&P 500 -3.7%. QQQ's -5.67% is from a secondary Friday close report. Extreme volatility supports both continuation risk and sharp short-covering potential. These are historical Friday prints, not fresh Saturday market movements.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the 08:29 EST assessment, an additional review of AP's November 21 closing recap, Reuters' November 20 week-ahead analysis and StoneX's November 20 semiconductor technical note finds no fresh US cash session or newly curated Open Watch catalyst. Reuters highlights the role of consumer spending and AI financing anxiety; StoneX's financial-conditions analysis reinforces the pre-existing bearish framework rather than proving a new weekend selloff. Open Watch remains 174 events. Bias, confidence and event risk are unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Disproportionate chip losses, negative breadth and high volatility support the bearish continuation scenario. StoneX's November 20 note discusses tightening financial conditions, but its historical conditional analysis is not a new synchronized market measurement. Sources disagree on Friday's precise VIX close, so the previously quoted 37.66 is source-attributed rather than treated as independently confirmed. The stale 4.94% 10Y and 4.65% 2Y yield pair implies +29 bp, not a live curve. FedWatch, VXN and maturity-aligned oil quotes remain unverified.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: a volatile reopening may produce an oversold bounce, with flash PMIs testing the growth and rates narrative. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Analog Devices/Dell earnings test semiconductor and technology demand. Wednesday November 25: PCE, GDP and the Fed Beige Book could reshape rate expectations and risk appetite. These are prospective scenarios. The baseline remains elevated downside risk unless QQQ and SOX/SMH rebound together with improving breadth and lower volatility.
editorial.bullCase: The extreme Friday drawdown could invite short-covering, especially if Monday PMIs and subsequent earnings are better than feared. A durable improvement needs synchronized QQQ/SOX/SMH strength, healthier advance-decline participation, falling VIX/VXN and verified easing in rate pressure.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's sharp chip underperformance and broad liquidation suggest rebounds may fail while volatility remains elevated. Weak PMI, consumer-confidence, AI-hardware guidance or inflation outcomes could deepen losses, but their impacts cannot be counted before publication and observed market response.
editorial.watchNext: Verify synchronized Monday QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX/SMH, VXN/VIX and breadth; paired Treasury yields with proper percent-to-basis-point scaling; CME FedWatch probabilities and contract-aligned Brent/WTI. Monitor Nov 23 PMIs, Nov 24 consumer confidence and ADI/Dell earnings, Nov 25 PCE/GDP/Beige Book, and any genuinely new curated Open Watch event.
